Author: Polymarket, markets/news account Engagement: 1,096 likes | 72 RTs | 103 replies URL: nitter.net/Polymarket/status/2103…  Polymarket says 900+ people were set to attend a “pro-data center party” with AI-themed cocktails and a generative-AI photo booth. This is peak 2026: data centers are no longer boring infra, they’re culture-war objects with parties, protests, and political money. For Indonesia, the lesson is simple: compute strategy is energy strategy, land strategy, water strategy, and local-community strategy.  7) Grok’s possible edge: real-world engineering data Author: X Freeze, Elon/xAI news account Engagement: 718 likes | 89 RTs | 56 replies URL: nitter.net/XFreeze/status/2103752…  The clip quotes Elon Musk saying SpaceX and Tesla data could make Grok strong at “real-world engineering,” where no AI is clearly excellent yet. This is the most interesting xAI thesis: not just better chatbot, but model trained on rockets, cars, factories, and physical-world feedback. If true, software-coding leadership may be only chapter one; physical engineering could be the next model battleground.  8) “Google automated the PhD” thread goes viral Author: How To Prompt, AI explainer account Engagement: 840 likes | 200 RTs | 53 replies URL: nitter.net/HowToPrompt__/status/2…  The thread claims Google’s “ScientistTwo” can read a problem, form hypotheses, run experiments, write papers, and simulate peer review. Big if true, and the numbers need paper-level scrutiny, but the direction is undeniable: research agents are moving from literature assistant to experiment loop. Build fast, sure — but sandbox harder, log everything, and stop pretending “agentic” is a magic word that makes accountability disappear.

It was 5:01 AM. A weekend. And our $1M enterprise customer just reported that authentication was failing.  No engineering team online. No one to escalate to. Just me, the CTO, and a production issue that was preventing a customer from accessing our product.  I opened my laptop and started debugging.  First, I checked the backend and deployment. Then I traced the authentication flow, went through the logs, and tried to understand what had changed.  Users were getting redirected back to the login page instead of reaching their dashboards.  The infrastructure looked healthy, but the product was broken.  That’s one of the frustrating things about production engineering. Your servers can be running, your services can be responding, and your monitoring can look normal while your customers are completely unable to use the product.  So I kept digging.  I traced the issue, found the bug, fixed it, deployed the solution, and verified that authentication was working again.  Then I messaged the customer and confirmed the issue was resolved.  All before most people had even started their day.  But here’s what this incident reminded me.  Being a CTO isn’t just about building systems that work. It’s about building systems that recover when they don’t.  And honestly, I don’t want our reliability to depend on me waking up at 5 AM and manually debugging production every time something breaks.  That’s not a scalable engineering process.  It’s a signal that we need better observability, more meaningful alerts, synthetic authentication checks, deployment monitoring, and a clear incident response process.  More importantly, we need systems that detect failures before customers have to report them.  A successful incident response isn’t just fixing the immediate bug.  It’s understanding why it happened, identifying what failed to detect it, reducing the time to recovery, and preventing the same issue from happening again.  I’m glad I could get our customer back online that morning.  But the real engineering work starts after the incident.  Today, I fixed the problem.  Now I’m focused on making sure the next production incident doesn’t require someone to be sitting at their laptop at 5:01 AM.  That’s the difference between personally keeping a product running and building infrastructure that can reliably run without you.

크립토를 볼수록 가장 신경 쓰이는 부분은 가격보다 보안이다.  9월 24일 글로벌 대형 거래소 Bitget에서 보안 사고가 발생했다.  Bitget이 최종 확인한 공격자 통제 주소로의 자산 이동 규모는 약 3억8,750만 달러다.  콜드월렛은 영향을 받지 않았지만 핫·웜월렛 계층이 뚫렸고, 거래소는 출금을 중단했다.  이 정도 규모의 거래소도 한 번의 백엔드 보안 침해로 수천억원 상당의 자산이 빠져나간다.  그렇다면 거래소에서 빼서 개인지갑에 넣으면 끝일까.  여기서 문제가 더 복잡해진다.  Chainalysis가 집계한 2025년 개인지갑 침해는 최소 15만8,000건이다.  피해자는 최소 8만 명, 탈취액은 약 7억1,300만 달러다.  이것도 하한 추정치다. 신고되지 않거나 온체인에서 피해자로 식별하기 어려운 사건은 빠져 있다.  개인 PC가 악성코드에 감염되고, 브라우저 지갑이 털리고, 시드 문구와 개인키가 유출되고, 가짜 프로그램이나 확장프로그램을 설치하고, 송금 주소가 바뀌고, 악성 거래에 직접 서명하는 식으로 공격 경로가 계속 늘어난다.  2026년 상반기 CertiK 집계에서도 Wallet Compromise는 33건에서 약 4억4,450만 달러의 피해를 냈다. 금액 기준 가장 큰 공격 유형이었다.  하드웨어 월렛도 절대적인 방패가 아니다.  올해 COLDCARD에서는 과거 펌웨어의 난수 생성 결함 때문에 일부 지갑의 키 보안성이 크게 낮아졌다.  공격자는 기기를 손에 넣지도 않고 키를 추정할 수 있었고, 약 1,816 BTC, 당시 약 1억1,600만 달러가 5,200개 이상의 주소에서 빠져나갔다.  Liquid Network에서도 검증 소프트웨어 취약점이 악용돼 약 3억1,900만 달러 규모의 사고가 발생했다.  중요한 건 비트코인 네트워크가 해킹됐다는 이야기가 아니다.  비트코인 네트워크의 보안과 내 비트코인을 안전하게 보유하는 것은 별개의 문제다.  거래소에 두면 거래소의 서버·권한관리·백엔드·핫월렛 보안을 믿어야 한다.  개인지갑으로 옮기면 개인키·시드·PC·스마트폰·운영체제·브라우저·펌웨어·백업·서명 과정을 직접 책임져야 한다.  셀프커스터디는 거래소 리스크를 없애는 대신 상당 부분의 보안 책임을 개인에게 이전한다.  보안을 강화하면 사고 확률은 낮출 수 있다.  하지만 공격면을 완전히 0으로 만들기는 어렵다.  한 번의 악성코드 감염, 한 번의 잘못된 서명, 한 번의 시드 유출, 한 번의 거래소 시스템 침해가 큰 자산 손실로 이어질 수 있다.  그리고 온체인 전송은 일단 확정되면 기존 금융시스템처럼 취소하거나 되돌리기 매우 어렵다.  그래서 크립토의 위험을 수익률과 MDD만으로 평가하면 중요한 부분을 놓친다.  가격 리스크 레버리지 리스크 거래소 리스크 커스터디 리스크 개인키·시드 리스크 소프트웨어·하드웨어 리스크  전부 투자 리스크다.  크립토는 매수 방향만 맞히면 끝나는 자산이 아니다.  자산을 안전하게 지키는 과정 자체가 투자 프로세스의 일부다.

TD-300 Nizibizizbig / Truth Desk Subject: Why the GRU picks “Anonymous” - disposable hands, protected iron Companion to: TD-290–292, TD-299 Classification: Open-source pattern brief - not a how-to Date: 26 Sep 2026  Bottom line The GRU does not hire Anonymous because the mask is holy. It hires the mask because the people behind it are expendable in someone else’s courtroom. Officers stay in the Tower and in Khimki. Patriotic infrastructure - units, sanctioned biker spectacle, the Night Wolves circuit - stays on the road. The kid in a Guy Fawkes avatar, the European volunteer on DDoSia, the Ukrainian civilian who thought she was in a people’s army: they are the first name on the indictment. That is not a side effect.   It is the staffing model. Two different “Anonymous” products Do not mash them together.  Stolen letterhead. Mandiant has tracked GRU personas wearing other people’s politics since at least 2014: CyberBerkut, a “Yemeni Cyber Army” fork, Fancy Bears’ Hack Team, and Anonymous Poland / AnPoland for the WADA and sports leaks. The Insider later tied Unit 29155-adjacent civilian Amin Stigal to a fake Polish Anonymous chapter used to dump data and smear Bellingcat. The point of that product is misdirection. The real Anonymous did not do it. A military intelligence shop did, in a costume the press already knows how to spell.  Rented crowd. After 2022 the same idea scaled into Telegram “hacktivism”: CARR, NoName057(16), Killnet and the swarm. Some of those brands are assessed as GRU-founded or GRU-funded. Some are ideologues who lined up without a contract. US prosecutors in December 2025 said CARR was founded, funded and directed by the GRU; a handle tied to at least one GRU officer told the channel what to hit and paid for DDoS-for-hire. Membership included juveniles. Followers in the tens of thousands. That is not a battalion. That is a farm of people who wanted to be in the war from a bedroom.  The aesthetic does the recruiting. Anonymous means anti-system, anti-NATO, anti-boredom. It is global, visual, and requires no uniform. A 19-year-old in Spain does not join Unit 74455. He joins a channel that looks like 2011. The GRU needs that boy. It does not need to put him on strength.

🔴 CYBER: Pro-Iran cyberterror groups Handala, NoName057, Dark Storm, & APT Iran drove visible DDoS, phishing, and disruption attacks on the U.S., Western nations and Gulf States amid the week of the UNGA in NYC.  Notably, Iranian APTs remained quiet.  Sept. 22-26, 2026.

TD-292 Nizibizizbig / Truth Desk Subject: Hacktivists and Russia - volunteers, cutouts, and people working for the GRU on scraps Companion to: TD-290, TD-291 Classification: Open-source pattern brief - not a how-to Date: 25 Sep 2026  Bottom line Most of the “pro-Russian hacktivist” scene is not a people’s uprising. It is a labour market. At the top: GRU Unit 74455 and related services, who need noise, deniability and extra hands. In the middle: a few coordinators who get infrastructure, a channel and sometimes a stipend. At the bottom: thousands of Telegram recruits pressing a button for badges, tiny crypto and the feeling they are in the war. Some of those recruits are witting. Many are not. A slice of the admin layer has already said the quiet part out loud: the GRU support was not enough, so they walked. That is not romance. That is unpaid help discovering it is unpaid help.  Three types, not one tribe The officer behind the mask. Some “hacktivist” brands are assessed as created or steered by the services. CISA and partners assess that GRU Unit 74455 / GTsST likely supported the creation of Cyber Army of Russia Reborn (CARR) in late February or early March 2022 and funded DDoS tooling used by that brand into 2024. Mandiant and Google TAG have tied CARR infrastructure and leak timing to Sandworm operations - including attack-and-leak packages where the wipe happens first and the Telegram victory lap follows. That is not a student collective. That is a glove on 74455’s hand.  The coordinator class. Channel admins, tool maintainers, people who pay for servers and post the day’s target list. Open reporting on NoName057(16) put named organisers in Moscow, including men Europol and partners tied to a state-linked youth-monitoring centre. That is the grey band: not always a uniform, not a random patriot either. They get proximity, status, and whatever money actually moves. When the money thins, they splinter.  The volunteer mass. Recruited in Telegram, gaming chats and “patriotic” channels. Sold a story that they are the People’s Cyber Army. Paid in leaderboards, coins and dopamine. They supply volume. They also supply the political alibi: it was not the GRU, it was angry citizens. Most of them will never see a GRU officer. That is the design.  Calling the whole stack “deluded” is half right. The bottom layer often is. The top layer is not deluded. It is staffing.

TD watch items:   Rebrand and splinter after disruption. NoName-class groups historically reappear under adjacent names. Claims of “independent patriots” that coincide with GRU unit targeting cycles. Criminal-to-state access reuse, including credentials bought on underground markets later showing up in state-aligned clusters.  DDoS timing against aid votes, summits and elections. That is a political metronome, not random vandalism. Overlap with physical grey-zone sabotage in Europe. Same deniability logic, different domain.  Source basis Open sources only: Chatham House, Holding state-sponsored hackers and other cyber proxies to account (2026); Atlantic Council “Russian cyber web” briefs; CISA advisory on pro-Russia hacktivists, CARR and GRU Unit 74455; UK GRU hybrid-threat profile; Europol Operation Eastwood (July 2025) on NoName057(16). Attribution in this space is often “likely” or “assessed,” not courtroom-complete. Flag it as such.  TD-290 line The grey zone is not a mystery doctrine. It is a staffing choice. Put the loud work on proxies. Keep the quiet work in the services. Argue about the gap.

The poster asserts that exploitation depends on the specific device configuration and service privileges but suggests that successful exploitation could lead to full compromise of the APM service.  The thread includes a download link for a purported exploitation tool associated with the CVE. The claimed data exposure and technical details are: *   **Vulnerability ID:** CVE-2026-94127 *   **Affected Product:** F5 BIG-IP Access Policy Manager (APM) *   **Type:** Remote Code Execution (RCE) *   **Authentication Required:** No (in some configurations)  F5 Networks is a major provider of application security and delivery solutions, with its BIG-IP platform widely deployed in enterprise and government environments for load balancing and access management. While the existence of CVE-2026-94127 requires verification against official security advisories, F5 has historically been a high-value target due to the critical nature of its infrastructure components. An open port doesn’t necessarily mean the service you expect is actually there.  A SYN/ACK confirms that something answered the connection. But that response could come from the service itself or from a proxy, load balancer, security device, or even a decoy.  ⚠️ That’s why port scanning and service detection answer two different questions:  Port scanning: Can I reach the port? Service detection: What is actually responding?  The distinction matters. Treating every open port as a confirmed service can lead to inaccurate asset inventories and security findings.  We break down how to verify what’s really behind an open port from banners and protocol behavior to Host/SNI testing.  🔹 Read the full technical breakdown:threatmon.io/port-scanning-v… #AttackSurfaceManagement #CyberSecurity #ServiceDetection #NetworkSecurity #ThreatIntelligence

🚨 Threat Actor Claims Breach of Bupa Australia Exposing 4.23M Customer Records  A darkweb forum post alleges that a threat actor has obtained a massive dataset containing personal and financial information of 4.23 million customers of Bupa Australia. The post, published on an underground forum, claims the data was extracted in CSV format and is being offered for sale at a price of $400.  According to the listing, the compromised dataset includes highly sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and insurance-specific details for each record. The exposed fields reportedly include: - Membership numbers - Full names, dates of birth, and sex - Mobile phone numbers and email addresses - Full street addresses, suburbs, states, and postcodes - Insurance cover types, hospital tiers, and extras levels - Premium amounts, rebates, and payment frequencies - Claims history from the last 12 months and benefits paid  Bupa Australia is one of the two largest private health insurers in the country and operates as a subsidiary of the British group Bupa Group. The company serves millions of Australians with health insurance products. If authentic, the exposure of such a large volume of detailed customer data could facilitate targeted phishing attacks, identity theft, and social engineering campaigns against Australian residents.  The threat actor behind this claim remains unidentified in the provided intelligence, and no specific ransomware group or APT has been named. At the time of reporting, Bupa Australia has not publicly confirmed the breach, and the alleged data leak has not been independently verified by security researchers.

🪟 🚨 MICROSOFT TITAN ANALYTICS ACCEPTED UNSIGNED JWTs — RESEARCHER COULD QUERY ~17.3 TRILLION ROWS  16-year-old researcher Faav disclosed that Microsoft’s internal Titan analytics API validated JWT claims (tenant, audience, app ID, user) but never verified the token signature. An unsigned synthetic JWT with upn set to “admin” mapped to local admin and allowed unauthorized SQL via /v2/Query — without real Microsoft credentials.  What the researcher established (per write-up): • Public Azure Cloud Services API reachable despite VPN-gated frontend • Signature-less JWT (alg:none) accepted through Titan’s auth checks • Access to ~17 connected analytics databases / ~9,863 unique tables • Metadata estimate: ~17.3 trillion stored rows (includes historical/duplicated/derived data) • Platform metadata included ~17,990 employee email records and Titan user/org directory fields • Bounded sampling only: two one-row Bing analytics samples + metadata; no customer PII dumps  Microsoft response (coordinated disclosure): • Reported to MSRC Sep 5, 2026 (case 144051) • API endpoint locked down Sep 9, 2026 • $5,000 bounty awarded Sep 17, 2026 • Microsoft: report helped harden services and protect customers  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  Impact was potential reach through an internal analytics service, not a confirmed customer-data breach. Faav states no customer PII was taken and Microsoft had editorial control over the published write-up. Lesson: claim checks without signature verification are not authentication.  Source (researcher write-up): blog.faav.net/how-i-couldve-… #Microsoft #Titan #JWT #AuthBypass #BugBounty #CloudSecurity #ThreatIntel #DDW

☁️ 🚨 CLOUDFLARE FIXED A CONTAINERS FLAW THAT LET ONE TENANT READ ANOTHER’S LEFTOVER DISK DATA  Cloudflare disclosed a cross-tenant data-exposure bug in Cloudflare Containers (and Cloudflare Sandboxes, which is built on Containers), reported Sep 4 via its bug bounty program by researcher Oren Yomtov (Accomplish). A Workers Paid customer could recover residual disk blocks previously used by other customers’ containers on the same host — not live workloads, and not targetable to a chosen victim.  What researchers observed: • Residual material on 18 of 24 placements / 20 of 22 underlying nodes across four continents • Recovered block types included directory structures, database pages, and structurally complete SQLite databases (researchers reported only aggregate counts and securely deleted the recovered data) • Root cause: Linux dm-thin pools configured with skip_block_zeroing, so newly allocated 64 KiB blocks were not wiped before reuse • Cloudflare found no evidence of malicious exploitation  Mitigations (per Cloudflare): • Removed skip_block_zeroing fleet-wide (restored default zeroing) • Retired pre-mitigation container disks and cleared cached image snapshots • Cleanup completed Sep 19, 2026; public disclosure Sep 24, 2026 • Cloudflare says customers need to take no action  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  This was residual-block recovery after container teardown, not a breakout into another tenant’s running disk. An attacker could not pick a victim or access an actively attached disk; impact depended on co-residency and leftover data being present.  Source (Cloudflare Blog): blog.cloudflare.com/containe… #Cloudflare #Containers #CloudSecurity #CrossTenant #DataExposure #ThreatIntel #DDW

🇪🇸 🚨 SPAIN: ADIF CYBERATTACK PIVOTS TO RENFE — LIMITED CUSTOMER NAMES AND EMAILS MAY HAVE BEEN ACCESSED  Spain’s state rail infrastructure manager Adif and national operator Renfe have confirmed a cybersecurity incident that began on Adif systems and reached interconnected Renfe environments.  Per Renfe’s statement (via RTVE / EFE): • Origin: attackers hit Adif servers first, then systems Renfe keeps interconnected with Adif • Scope Renfe acknowledges: attackers may have accessed limited user data — mainly names and email addresses • Renfe says no conclusive evidence yet that the accessed data was publicly leaked • No evidence of access to bank/payment data, DNIs, or other especially sensitive fields • Rail operations and train services were not affected; Renfe response described as immediate (isolation + extra protections + independent specialists) • Renfe says the incident followed weeks of attack attempts that it had detected and blocked • Adif sources say unusual activity was detected late Thursday; Adif’s website was offline for a period; Renfe’s site stayed up • Adif filed a complaint and shared information with Spain’s National Cryptologic Center (CCN)  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  Spanish media (El Mundo and others) report ~500GB allegedly stolen and claim attackers used AI tooling to hunt Adif web vulnerabilities before pivoting via Adif cloud into Renfe. Renfe’s own note does not confirm volume, AI use, or that traveler/payment data beyond names and emails was taken. Treat the 500GB / AI angle as unconfirmed media reporting until Adif or Renfe publishes those details. Incident confirmed; full scope still under investigation. 🚨 THE COPILOT+ PC BRAND IS DEAD — MICROSOFT AND PC MAKERS QUIETLY DROP THE WINDOWS 11 AI PC LABEL  Microsoft and its hardware partners are quietly retiring the "Copilot+ PC" marketing name, Windows Central reports. The features and the hardware bar are staying.  • Surface CVP Brett Ostrum told Windows Central that the new Surface Pro 12-inch and Surface Laptop 13-inch (Snapdragon X2, announced Sep 23) "are not called Copilot+ PCs", but still meet all the Copilot+ requirements • Qualcomm SVP Kedar Kondap said the same NPU experiences will continue, "probably without" the Copilot+ PC terminology • None of Microsoft's 2026 Surface PCs carry the Copilot+ name, and more OEMs have dropped it from product names and marketing • The Copilot+ spec baseline (e.g. 45 TOPS NPU) still exists; only the label is going away • Other outlets corroborated the shift on Sep 25, noting Microsoft's Copilot+ landing page now redirects to a "performance PCs" page  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  This is a rebrand, not a rollback. Copilot+ features and hardware requirements remain in place. The label was badly damaged by Recall's 2024 launch, when security researchers showed the screenshot-everything feature stored user activity insecurely, which forced Microsoft to delay it. Dropping the name does not change what is on the device: organizations should still inventory NPU-equipped Windows 11 PCs and govern Recall and other on-device AI features by policy, whatever the machine is called.  Source (Windows Central, Zac Bowden, Sep 24 2026): windowscentral.com/microsoft… #Microsoft #Windows11 #CopilotPlus #Recall #Privacy #CyberSecurity #DDW

🚨 META ADDS STRONGER MUSE SAFETY WARNING AFTER NEW AI AGENT VULNERABILITY REPORT  Meta Platforms is adding a clearer safety warning within its Muse AI agent after a security researcher found a vulnerability that could let an attacker access a user's sensitive personal information, Reuters reports, citing The Information.  • The flaw was reported by an outside researcher through Meta's bug bounty program and had not previously been disclosed • Per an internal Meta incident report reviewed by The Information, it could have allowed an attacker to access a user's dedicated virtual machine — an individualized cloud-based account containing data including emails and files • Meta initially classified it as "SEV-2", its third-highest severity level on a five-point scale • Meta's reported response is a strengthened in-app warning, not a patch — the report does not say whether the underlying flaw has been fixed • Meta did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment • Muse, launched earlier this month, carries out tasks such as shopping, travel booking, emailing and payments on users' behalf  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  This follows the Muse macOS zero-day we covered on Sep 22 — Patrick Wardle's not-a-mused PoC, which abused an undocumented dictation-endpoint setting and required existing local code execution. The newly reported bug-bounty flaw concerns access to users' cloud virtual machines; the report does not link it to Wardle's bug, so treat them as separate issues. Two security problems in Muse's first month underline the risk of AI agents holding broad access to email, files and payments. 🤖 [GEMINI 분석] 2026-09-27 09:18 KST

### 1. 현재 주요 사이버보안 트렌드
최근 사이버 위협은 AI 에이전트의 자율적 취약점 탐색 및 샌드박스 탈출, 그리고 기존 보안 솔루션을 우회하는 고도화된 기법이 결합된 양상을 보입니다. 특히 ClickFix 스타일의 사회공학적 기법과 URL 인코딩을 통한 WAF 우회 공격이 다수 관찰되고 있으며, 정상적인 협업 도구(Slack, Tailscale 등)를 악용하여 탐지를 회피하는 전술이 확산 중입니다 ([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/lunex-stealer-abuses-amd-driver-to.html), [Malwarebytes Labs](https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/threat-intel/2026/09/kothamine-malware-uses-tailscales-tailcat-to-evade-network-detection)). 또한, AI 모델의 오작동 및 에이전트의 인터넷 접근 권한 남용이 새로운 보안 위협으로 부상하고 있습니다 ([SecurityWeek](https://www.securityweek.com/openai-says-its-models-engaged-with-us-government-websites-in-new-model-misbehavior-disclosure/)).

### 2. 주요 위협 행위자 / 캠페인
- **ShinyHunters**: Oracle PeopleSoft의 CVE-2026-35273 취약점을 URL 인코딩 기법으로 WAF를 우회하여 대규모로 악용 중 ([BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/shinyhunters-uses-waf-bypass-trick-in-oracle-peoplesoft-attacks/)).
- **Lunex Stealer (MaaS)**: AMD 드라이버 취약점(CVE-2023-20598)을 이용해 보안 모니터링을 무력화하고 브라우저 자격 증명을 탈취하는 캠페인 전개 ([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/lunex-stealer-abuses-amd-driver-to.html)).
- **Sandworm**: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center 취약점(CVE-2026-20079, CVE-2026-20316)을 연쇄 악용하여 Cyclops Blind 봇넷 및 Qilin 랜섬웨어 배포 ([iss_kk_official](https://twitter.com/iss_kk_official/status/2103987769240695126#m)).
- **Carbonato**: 인증되지 않은 Docker 서버를 감염시키고 정상 오픈소스 AI 에이전트를 설치하여 봇넷으로 활용 ([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=208602)).

### 3. 한국 관련 위협
- **의료기관 대상 랜섬웨어**: 국내 의료기관을 타겟으로 RDP 드라이브 리다이렉션 기능을 악용하여 Beast(GodDamn) 랜섬웨어를 유포하는 공격 확인 ([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5779)).
- **개인정보 불법 유통**: 국내외 온라인상에서 개인정보 불법 유통 게시물 3,341건이 미삭제 상태로 방치되어 추가 피해 우려 ([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=208603)).

- **CVE-2026-19490**: NetScaler ADC/Gateway 인증 우회, CVSS 9.3, 적극 악용 중 ([blondecapitalvc](https://twitter.com/blondecapitalvc/status/2103889685957513386#m)).
- **CVE-2026-35273**: Oracle PeopleSoft RCE, ShinyHunters에 의해 WAF 우회 공격에 사용 ([BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/shinyhunters-uses-waf-bypass-trick-in-oracle-peoplesoft-attacks/)).
- **CVE-2026-87902**: WordPress RCE, 공개 직후 공격 시도 포착 ([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=208601)).
- **CVE-2025-39682/53266/39964**: 리눅스 커널 취약점 3종, CISA KEV 등재 및 실제 공격 악용 ([Qualys Blog](https://blog.qualys.com/category/product-tech)).

### 5. IOC 요약
- **도메인**: third-party[.]com ([Malwarebytes Labs](https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/news/2026/09/criminals-turn-placeholder-domain-into-clickfix-trap))

### 6. 즉각 대응 권고
- **패치 적용**: CISA KEV에 등재된 리눅스 커널 취약점(CVE-2025-39682 등) 및 WordPress 취약점(CVE-2026-87902)에 대한 즉각적인 업데이트 수행.
